examples.title: Launch an Incogniton profile with Playwright and take a screenshot
examples.question: How do I automate Incogniton with Playwright?
questions: How do I connect Playwright to an Incogniton profile?
How do I take a screenshot with the Incogniton SDK?
examples.summary: The minimal, self-contained starting point: check the profile is Ready, launch it through the official Node.js SDK, connect Playwright over CDP, use the profile's persistent default context, verify a page, save a screenshot and stop the profile gracefully.
examples.expectedResult: Prints `PASS: <Chrome version> rendered the fixture; screenshot saved to output/launch-profile-and-screenshot/<timestamp>/screenshot.png` and `Profile status after cleanup: Ready`; exit code 0.
examples.lifecycle: Launches the profile itself and stops it at the end: closes its own tab, sends CDP Browser.close so Chrome flushes storage, then waits until the app reports Ready (falls back to profile.stop() after ~20 s).

failures.cause: No profile configured.
failures.fix: npm run profiles -- list, then npm run setup -- --profile-id <id>.

failures.cause: The profile is already open (in the app or another script).
failures.fix: Close it in the Incogniton app and retry.

failures.cause: Desktop app not running, not logged in, API disabled, other port, or plan without automation.
failures.fix: Run npm run doctor.

examples.title: Fill and submit a form in an Incogniton profile with Playwright
examples.question: How do I click buttons and fill forms in an Incogniton profile?
questions: How do I use Playwright locators with Incogniton?
examples.summary: Fills a text field, selects an option, ticks a checkbox and submits a deterministic local form using semantic locators (getByLabel, getByRole) and Playwright's auto-waiting, then asserts the confirmation text.
examples.expectedResult: `click-and-fill-form: PASSED` with `Form submitted and verified: "Submitted: Ada Lovelace (Pro plan)"`; before-submit.png and after-submit.png in the run directory.
examples.lifecycle: Launches and stops the profile (graceful close, wait for Ready). The run fails with exit code 5 instead of taking over a profile that is already open.

failures.symptom: Timeout waiting for the status text
failures.cause: The form did not reach the expected state (selector or data changed).
failures.fix: Open failure-*.png in the run directory and adjust the locators.

examples.title: Keep cookies, localStorage and IndexedDB between Incogniton automation runs
examples.question: How do I preserve cookies and localStorage in Incogniton automation?
questions: Why are my cookies lost after stopping an Incogniton profile?
How do I reuse a logged-in session in Incogniton?
examples.summary: Proves persistence across two separate processes: run 1 writes a cookie, a localStorage value and an IndexedDB record on a fixed local origin and closes the browser gracefully; run 2 relaunches the same profile and reads them back. Also shows that browser.newContext() does not see the profile's storage.
examples.expectedResult: Two runs: `reuse-profile-session-write: PASSED` then `reuse-profile-session-verify: PASSED` with `Cookie, localStorage and IndexedDB values survived a full profile stop and relaunch.`
examples.lifecycle: Each phase launches and stops the profile. The graceful close (CDP Browser.close) matters: profile.stop() terminates Chrome, and cookies/localStorage written shortly before can be lost (verified). Storage belongs to an origin, so FIXTURE_PORT must stay the same between runs.

failures.cause: The browser was terminated (profile.stop/force-stop) before Chrome flushed storage, or FIXTURE_PORT changed between runs.
failures.fix: Shut down via Browser.close and wait for Ready (as the helpers do); keep FIXTURE_PORT stable.

failures.symptom: verify fails on a cloud-synced profile after switching devices
failures.cause: Local and cloud copies differ.
failures.fix: Resolve the sync state in the app; the starter never forces local or cloud.

examples.title: Automate same-origin and cross-origin iframes in Incogniton with Playwright
examples.question: How do I automate an iframe in an Incogniton profile?
questions: How do I click inside a cross-origin iframe with Playwright?
examples.summary: Waits for iframes that are inserted after a delay, clicks a button inside a same-origin frame, types into a cross-origin frame (different port), and verifies the frame posted a message to the parent page.
examples.expectedResult: `interact-with-iframe: PASSED` with `Clicked inside the same-origin frame (Count: 2) and sent a message from the cross-origin frame to the parent.`

failures.symptom: Fixture port 47812 is in use by another program
failures.cause: Port conflict.
failures.fix: Set FIXTURE_CROSS_ORIGIN_PORT in .env.

examples.title: Control a canvas game with keyboard and mouse in Incogniton (Playwright)
examples.question: How do I automate a canvas game in an Incogniton profile?
questions: How do I send arrow keys to a canvas with Playwright?
How do I click canvas coordinates correctly when the canvas is scaled?
examples.summary: Plays one round of a deterministic canvas coin-collector: converts canvas coordinates to page coordinates from the element's bounds, clicks START, focuses the canvas, and runs an observe/act loop with key down/up presses until all coins are collected. Observation is screenshot-based by default (pixel colours), cross-checked against fixture-only state.
examples.expectedResult: `control-canvas-game: PASSED` with `Round complete (Round complete: 3/3 coins in 34 moves) using pixels observation ...`; started.png and complete.png show the canvas.

failures.cause: Colours changed (e.g. a forced dark mode or colour profile) or the canvas is covered.
failures.fix: Check started.png; adjust PLAYER_COLOR/COIN_COLOR or use --observe state for the fixture.

failures.symptom: canvas did not receive keyboard focus
failures.cause: Something overlays the canvas at the click point.
failures.fix: Inspect started.png; click an uncovered canvas area.

examples.title: Run multiple Incogniton profiles concurrently with Playwright
examples.question: How do I run multiple Incogniton profiles concurrently?
questions: How do I automate several Incogniton profiles in parallel?
examples.summary: Runs the same form workflow in a list of distinct profiles with a small concurrency limit. Each worker owns its launch, context, output directory, result and shutdown; duplicate IDs are rejected and a failed job fails the run.
examples.expectedResult: One PASS line per profile and `All N profile jobs passed (concurrency 2).`; workers.json and one directory per profile in the run directory. Exit code 1 if any job failed.
examples.lifecycle: Each worker stops its own profile as soon as it finishes. A host-local lock file prevents two processes in this checkout from launching the same profile; it is not a distributed lock.

failures.cause: The same profile cannot run twice at once.
failures.fix: Pass distinct IDs.

failures.symptom: You have reached your profile-launch limit for this period.
failures.cause: Plan/account launch limit.
failures.fix: Lower the number of runs or check your plan.

examples.title: Attach Playwright to an Incogniton profile that is already running
examples.question: How do I connect to an existing Incogniton profile without restarting it?
questions: Can I attach to an already open Incogniton profile?
examples.summary: Attaches to a profile browser started earlier by `npm run session -- start` (which records its CDP endpoint), does work in a new tab, detaches and verifies the browser is still running. The Incogniton API does not return the endpoint of a profile that is already open, so attaching to a profile opened manually in the app is not possible.
examples.expectedResult: `attach-to-running-profile: PASSED` with `... detached. Browser still running (status Launched).`
examples.lifecycle: Never launches or stops anything: it only closes its own tab and disconnects. `npm run session -- stop` stops the browser that `session start` launched, and refuses to stop browsers without a session record.

failures.cause: The browser was not started by `npm run session -- start`.
failures.fix: Start it with that command, or pass --cdp-url from your own launcher.

failures.cause: The recorded browser was closed.
failures.fix: npm run session -- stop (clears the record), then start again.

examples.title: Create and delete a temporary Incogniton profile with the Node.js SDK
examples.question: How do I create an Incogniton profile from code?
questions: What is the minimal payload for Incogniton profile creation?
How do I delete only the profiles my automation created?
examples.summary: Creates a profile with the minimal verified payload (only general_profile_information.profile_name), records the returned profile_browser_id, uses it, and deletes exactly that profile during cleanup unless --keep-profile is passed.
examples.expectedResult: `create-and-clean-up-profile: PASSED` with `Created <id>, rendered the fixture ...`, log line `deleted profile <id>` and `cleanup <id>: ok`.
examples.lifecycle: Deletes only IDs recorded in .incogniton/created-profiles.json. If deletion fails the run reports a LEFTOVER and exit code 8; `npm run profiles -- delete-created --yes` retries.

failures.symptom: No permission to create profiles in this group
failures.cause: Team role permissions.
failures.fix: Use an account/role allowed to create profiles.

failures.cause: Delete failed (permissions, sync).
failures.fix: npm run profiles -- delete-created --yes

examples.title: Extract a paginated table to JSON in an Incogniton profile
examples.question: How do I scrape a paginated table with Playwright in Incogniton?
examples.summary: Reads every page of a paginated table, waits for each page to render before reading (no stale reads), stops when Next is disabled, validates count/uniqueness/values and writes products.json.
examples.expectedResult: `extract-paginated-data: PASSED` with `Extracted 25 products from 3 pages to products.json.`

failures.cause: Read before the next page rendered.
failures.fix: Wait for a page-specific condition (as the example does) before reading.

examples.title: Upload and download files in an Incogniton profile with Playwright
examples.question: How do I upload and download files with Playwright in Incogniton?
examples.summary: Uploads a generated file through a file input with setInputFiles and downloads a CSV via a link with waitForEvent('download'), verifying both. Downloads work in the profile's default context over CDP.
examples.expectedResult: `upload-and-download-files: PASSED` with `Uploaded upload.txt (verified by the page) and downloaded report.csv (45 bytes, content verified).`

failures.cause: The click did not start a download (e.g. a new tab opened instead).
failures.fix: Check failure-*.png; handle page.waitForEvent('popup') if the site opens a tab.

examples.title: Mock and block network requests in an Incogniton profile with Playwright
examples.question: How do I intercept or mock network requests in Incogniton automation?
examples.summary: Uses page.route() to replace an API response with a fixture value and to block a tracking pixel, and observes requests with page.on('request').
examples.lifecycle: Launches and stops the profile. Routes apply to this page only.

examples.title: Launch an Incogniton profile with Puppeteer and take a screenshot
examples.question: How do I automate Incogniton with Puppeteer?
questions: How do I connect Puppeteer to an Incogniton profile?
examples.summary: Self-contained Puppeteer version of the screenshot example: launch through the official Node.js SDK, puppeteer.connect({ browserURL, defaultViewport: null }), verify, screenshot, graceful stop.
examples.expectedResult: `PASS: Chrome/<version> rendered the fixture; screenshot saved to output/puppeteer-launch-profile-and-screenshot/<timestamp>/screenshot.png` and `Profile status after cleanup: Ready`.
examples.lifecycle: Puppeteer's browser.close() on a connected browser sends Browser.close (graceful stop); browser.disconnect() would leave it running. The example waits for Ready afterwards.

failures.cause: Already open.
failures.fix: Close it in the app first.

examples.title: Keep cookies and storage between Incogniton runs with Puppeteer
examples.question: How do I keep a Puppeteer session logged in across Incogniton runs?
examples.summary: Puppeteer version of the persistence proof: write cookie/localStorage/IndexedDB in one process, verify after relaunch in another.
examples.lifecycle: In Puppeteer, browser.newPage() uses the default (persistent) context; browser.createBrowserContext() would be isolated.

examples.title: Take screenshots with the Incogniton Python SDK and Playwright
examples.question: How do I take screenshots using the Incogniton Python SDK?
questions: How do I use Incogniton with Playwright for Python?
examples.summary: Python (asyncio) version: launch via the official `incogniton` PyPI SDK, connect_over_cdp, use browser.contexts[0], verify the fixture, screenshot, graceful stop, result.json.
examples.expectedResult: `python-launch-profile-and-screenshot: PASSED` and `cleanup <id>: ok via graceful, final status Ready`.
examples.lifecycle: Same lifecycle as the TypeScript helpers (examples/python/starter_common.py).

failures.cause: incogniton 0.3.0 has a fixed 35 s HTTP timeout; a slow (cloud-synced) launch can exceed it.
failures.fix: Retry once the profile is synced, or launch it once from the app.

examples.title: Keep cookies and localStorage between runs with the Incogniton Python SDK
examples.question: How do I preserve cookies with Incogniton and Playwright for Python?
examples.summary: Python version of the persistence proof across two processes.
examples.lifecycle: Graceful close via CDP Browser.close before each process exits.

examples.title: Automate an Incogniton profile with Selenium in Python
examples.question: How do I use Selenium with Incogniton?
questions: How do I get a WebDriver URL for an Incogniton profile?
examples.summary: Launches the profile through the app's Selenium grid (automation.launch_selenium_custom), connects webdriver.Remote to the returned URL (no local chromedriver), fills and submits the fixture form, screenshots, and ends with driver.quit(), after which the app stops the browser.
examples.expectedResult: `python-selenium-launch-profile-and-screenshot: PASSED` with `Selenium filled and submitted the form ...` and `cleanup <id>: ok via webdriver-quit, final status Ready`.
examples.lifecycle: driver.quit() ends the WebDriver session; the app then stops the browser. Whether that shutdown flushes very recent cookie/localStorage writes was not verified for Selenium.

failures.symptom: Automation service is being installed, please try again in a moment
failures.cause: The app downloads its Selenium server after login.
failures.fix: Wait and retry.

failures.symptom: Navigation did not complete: timeout: Timed out receiving message from renderer (exit 10)
failures.cause: Known intermittent issue on the Incogniton Selenium path: on the test host roughly 1 in 3 launches had a first navigation that never completed (data: URLs were not affected; the CDP path never showed it).
failures.fix: Run again. Prefer the Python Playwright example for unattended work until the product issue is fixed.
